chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatari, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the menstruating woman who sees the sign of purity, and her husband copulates with her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem, and the ritual bath (ghusl) is more beloved to me.'

key_terms.أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ: More beloved to me (indicating preference/premium virtue)
key_terms.الطُّهْر: Purity (the sign that menstruation has ended)
key_terms.الْغُسْل: Ritual bath (full body washing required after menstruation)
key_terms.لَا بَأْس: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a husband to have intercourse with his wife if she sees the end of her period but hasn't washed yet?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies that the onset of purity marks the end of the prohibition, making intercourse valid even before the ritual bath (ghusl) is completed, though he expresses a preference for it. This ruling highlights the distinction between the state of ritual impurity (hady) and the formal act of purification in Shia fiqh, emphasizing that the physical sign of purity lifts the ban immediately. The preference for ghusl reflects the spiritual and practical benefits of full ritual cleanliness before marital intimacy.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Salma Bin Al Khattab, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Al Tatary, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Ali Bin Yaqteen, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the menstruating woman who sees the purity and her husband copulates with her. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem, and the washing is more beloved to me’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Salmah ibn al-Khattab from Ali ibn al-Hassan al-Tatariy from Muhammad ibn abu Hamzah from Ali ibn Yaqtin who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman experiencing Hayd (menses) who finds herself clean and her husband goes to bed with her. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful but taking Ghusl (bath) is more likeable to me.’”
